title: Minimum Wage Adelaide: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Salary with Tax and Super
description: Learn how to convert minimum wage Adelaide rates to annual, fortnightly, and take-home pay. Includes tax, Medicare, and superannuation for 2026-27.
salarySummary: For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (38-hour week), the annual gross salary is approximately $52,265, with super and tax estimated on top.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual salary from my hourly rate in Adelaide?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by your usual weekly hours (for full-time, assume 38 hours) and then by 52 weeks. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour gives $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,265.44 gross per year. This formula works for any hourly rate, but remember it assumes the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage in Adelaide for 2026-27?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission applies across Australia, including Adelaide. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour for adult employees, or $1004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual workers receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. Some industry awards may set higher minimum rates, so check your specific award.

faqs.q: How much tax and Medicare will I pay on the minimum wage in Adelaide?
faqs.a: Using 2026-27 resident tax rates, a single person earning $52,265 pays no tax on the first $18,200, then 15% on the next $26,800 ($4,020), and 30% on the remaining $7,265 ($2,179.50), totalling about $6,199.50. The Medicare levy is 2% of taxable income, around $1,045.30. After tax and Medicare, take-home pay is roughly $45,020 per year, or $1,731 per fortnight. These are estimates; your exact amount depends on your circumstances.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: From Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

If you earn an hourly wage in Adelaide and want to know what that means as an annual salary, fortnightly pay, or take-home amount after tax and super, you have come to the right place. This guide explains the conversion process, the role of the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and how superannuation and tax affect your pocket. We focus on the **minimum wage Adelaide** context, but the principles apply to any hourly rate.

### How the Conversion Works

The standard formula to estimate your annual gross salary is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee, we assume a 38-hour week, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This is the standard for full-time work under most awards and the National Employment Standards. If you work part-time or different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The formula gives a base figure before any deductions or additions.

For example, on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,265.44 per year (gross)

This is the starting point for calculating tax, Medicare, and super. To find your fortnightly pay, divide the annual figure by 26 (or multiply your weekly pay by 2). For the minimum wage, fortnightly gross is about $2,009.80.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The **minimum wage Adelaide** workers receive is the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission, unless a specific industry award applies. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for adult employees, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, many industries have award rates that are higher. For example, hospitality, retail, and construction awards often set higher minimums. Always check your award or agreement to see if you are entitled to more than the national minimum. You can find award pay guides on the Fair Work Ombudsman website. For more details on minimum rates, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.

### Casual Loading

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements. The casual rate for the National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using our [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. **Do not** type a rate that already includes casual loading; the tool adds it automatically. For more on casual rates, visit our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

### Superannuation

Superannuation (super) is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution to your retirement fund. For the minimum wage example:

$52,265.44 × 12% = $6,271.85 per year in super

This amount is paid into your super account and is not included in your take-home pay. Learn more about how super interacts with your salary on our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Tax and Medicare

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate your tax and Medicare levy using the 2026-27 resident tax rates. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Income between $18,201 and $45,000 is taxed at 15%, then 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income (with possible reductions for low-income earners).

For a single resident earning $52,265.44:
- Tax: $0 on first $18,200; 15% on $26,800 ($4,020); 30% on $7,265.44 ($2,179.63) = total tax $6,199.63
- Medicare levy: 2% of $52,265.44 = $1,045.31
- Total deductions: $7,244.94
- Estimated annual take-home: $45,020.50
- Fortnightly take-home: approximately $1,731.56

These figures are estimates. Your actual tax may vary if you have a HELP debt, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

### Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/), also the home page, lets you enter your base hourly rate. It then calculates annual, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading. The tool uses the same formula (hourly × hours × 52) and assumes a 38-hour week unless you change it. Remember, the results are estimates and do not include penalty rates, allowances, or unpaid overtime. Always refer to your pay slip for exact figures.

### Conclusion

Understanding your pay from hourly to annual is straightforward with the formula hourly × hours per week × 52. For the **minimum wage Adelaide** context, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour gives an annual gross of about $52,265. After adding super (12% on top) and deducting tax and Medicare, your take-home is around $45,020 per year. Whether you are comparing a salary offer or planning your budget, this conversion helps you see the full picture. For more reference tables and data, visit our [reference tables](/data) page.
